words.etymon: renewal of pie-lex-wiHros (packet mapping to *perh₃- is wrong; puruṣa- has no secure PIE etymon)
renewal of the human member (Osc. famel; derivation from *dʰeh₁- uncertain)

cognate: Ved. paśu- = Lat. pecus/pecua = Umbr. pequo = Av. pasu- (*péḱu); the human member is *wiHro- in Av. vīra-, Umbr. ueiro, Ved. vīra- (support), renewed by Ved. puruṣa- and Lat. pastores/familia; the protective verb Ved. trā- = Av. θrā- (θrāθrāi) *treh₂-.
drift_or_renewal: In the packet passages the 'men' slot is renewed: Ved. puruṣa- (beside inherited vīra- in AVP 19.56, AVŚ 11.1, RV 1.114.8), Lat. pastores / familia (beside Umbr. ueiro which keeps *wiHro-). Renewal by the everyday word for 'person/servant' is expected in prose (Cato) and in late Vedic; the pecus member never changes.
shared_syntax: Coordinated pair (asyndetic or with -que/ca/aut) 'men (and) livestock' as object of a protecting or harming verb in a prayer or rule: Ved. trāyantām ... puruṣaṃ paśum; Av. θrāθrāi pasuuā̊ vīraiiā̊; Lat. pastores pecuaque salua seruassis; Umbr. ueiro pequo ... salua seritu; legal variant Lat. aut pastores aut pecus ... damni dederit.
context: AVŚ 8.7.22: plants asked to protect, in this village, cow, horse, man, livestock; AVŚ 11.2.18: the five paśavo of Paśupati include puruṣa; Cato 149.2: the buyer's/owner's people and livestock as one liable unit in a grazing contract, and Cato 141.2 (support) the same pair as the object of Mars's protection; Umbrian and Avestan show it as the object of 'keep safe / protect'. Same domain (the farm/village's human and animal holdings), same polarity (protect vs harm). Not generic: the specific binomial with an inherited *peḱu member and a protection verb recurs in four branches, with a cognate verb in Indo-Iranian (trā-/θrā-) and a cognate verb pair inside Italic (salua seruassis = salua seritu).
phrase: *wiHrōs péḱu (pie-lex-wiHros + pie-lex-pekju), object of *treh₂- / *ser(w)- 'protect, keep safe'

cognate: Gk στεῖρα βοῦς = Ved. starī́- gáv- (RV, support): both members cognate (*stériH- + *gʷṓw-); Lat. sterilis is the Italic derivative of the same root.
drift_or_renewal: Latin keeps the adjective (sterilis, here of humans) but not the fixed NP with bos in this corpus; the Vedic NP is attested only in support passages, so the Indo-Iranian side is not anchored in the packet.
shared_syntax: Attributive adjective + noun 'barren cow' (Gk acc. στεῖραν βοῦν; Ved. acc. staryàm ... gā́m).
context: A pastoral-ritual category: in the Odyssey the best barren cow is vowed as sacrifice to the dead; in the RV the Aśvins make the barren cow (staryàm gā́m) swell with milk for Śayu. Both treat the barren cow as a marked animal. Lucretius 4.1240 uses the cognate adjective for sterile couples in a passage on fertility rites. Exact two-member cognate NP in Greek and Vedic is unlikely to be chance, though it may be a lexical term rather than a poetic formula.

cognate: Ved. ūrdhvá- = Av. ərəδβa- = Gk ὀρθός (*h₃r̥dʰwó-) with *steh₂- (Ved. tasthau/tiṣṭha, Av. hištəṇta, Gk ἑσταότων/στῆ).
drift_or_renewal: Latin renews the adjective with rectus (arduus, the cognate, means 'steep') and keeps stare.
shared_syntax: Predicative adjective agreeing with the subject of 'stand' (ūrdhvás tasthau; ὀρθῶν ἑσταότων; ərəδβā̊ hištəṇta; rectam stare).
context: Only partly congruent: AVŚ 9.9.19 / RV 1.164.10 and Yt 13.76 are cosmogonic (a being 'stood upright' at the creation), Il. 18.246 is an assembly standing, Cato a post standing vertical. 'Stand upright' is a natural, compositional phrase, so inheritance as a phrase (rather than independent combination of inherited words) is hard to prove; the Indo-Iranian pair is the strongest part.

cognate: Only the verb: Ved. bhar- = Gk φέρω (*bʰer-), with 'earth' as subject and crops/goods/creatures as object.
drift_or_renewal: The earth noun differs everywhere (Ved. bhūmi-/pṛthivī-, Gk ἄρουρα/γαῖα); a cognate earth word *dʰéǵʰōm (Gk χθών, Ved. kṣam-) is not used in these passages.
context: Both are blessings of fertility: Hes. Op. 117 the golden age (earth bore fruit unbidden), Op. 232 and Od. 19.111 the just king's land; AVŚ 12.1 (Pṛthivī hymn) the earth who bears plants, creatures and wealth, asked to grant cows and food. The image is natural and may be independent, so this is a weak lead.

words.etymon: táwros (renewal of the 'bull' word; Ved. vṛṣan in context)

cognate: Only *gʷṓws (gavām / βόεσσι); the 'bull' words (vṛṣa- vs ταῦρος) and the superlatives (uttama- vs ἔξοχος) are not cognate.
drift_or_renewal: All key terms renewed; the match is of figure, not wording.
shared_syntax: God (Indra / Zeus) makes (kṛṇu, karat / θῆκε) the king outstanding like the bull among the herd: Ved. ekavṛṣam janānām ... rājñām uttamam; Gk ταῦρος ... βόεσσι μεταπρέπει ... ἔξοχον ἡρώεσσιν.
context: Both are royal-consecration or royal-praise contexts (AVŚ 4.22 is a hymn for the king's supremacy; Il. 2.480-3 Zeus makes Agamemnon pre-eminent that day). The king-as-bull simile is widespread, so this is typological at best.
phrase: god + *dʰeh₁-/kʷer- 'make' + king as the bull (pre-eminent) among cattle/men

cognate: Lat. pecua/pecus = Ved. paśu- (support; in AVŚ 4.21 the cattle are the addressees) = Umbr. pequo = Av. pasu- (*péḱu); the human member *wiHro- survives in Ved. vīra- (RV 1.114.8), Umbr. ueiro, Av. vīra-.
drift_or_renewal: Packet anchors renew both members in places: Ved. go- for paśu-, Lat. pastores/familia for *wiHro-; the averting verbs are not cognate (Ved. pari-vṛj, dūraṃ nī vs Lat. prohibere, defendere, auerruncare, salua seruare = Umbr. salua seritu).
shared_syntax: Prayer to a dangerous, disease-sending god (Mars pater / Rudra) to keep harm away from the household's men and cattle: Lat. morbos ... prohibessis defendas auerruncesque ... pastores pecuaque salua seruassis; Ved. pari vo rudrasya hetir vṛṇaktu (to the cows); rudrasya hetiṃ dūraṃ nayatu gobhyaḥ; RV 1.114.8 mā naḥ góṣu ... vīrā́n mā ... vadhīḥ.
context: Both are agrarian apotropaic prayers: Cato's suovetaurilia lustration of the farm to Mars, AVŚ 4.21 (cow hymn) and AVP 19.14 asking that Rudra's missile avoid / be led away from the cows. Mars and Rudra share the profile of an ambivalent god who both threatens and protects herds and men; the human+livestock pair as object, with inherited *peḱu, recurs in Umbrian and Avestan. The same formula as R4's P-4c5b claim, anchored here in the prayer itself.
phrase: *wiHrōs péḱu (pie-lex-wiHros + pie-lex-pekju) 'men (and) cattle' as object of a prayer that a god avert harm

cognate: Gen. pl. of *h₁wésu- 'good (things)' with a 'give' word, gods as givers: Ved. dātā́ vásūnām = Av. vohunąm dātārō = Gk (θεοί) δωτῆρες ἐάων (agent noun *deh₃-tor- + *h₁wésu-, support); in the packet Ved. vásu + dhā- (dhatta vasūni, vasu-dhāna-).
drift_or_renewal: In the packet's Greek line the goods are renewed (ὄλβια for ἐάων) with δίδωμι; in the Vedic packet lines the verb is *dʰeh₁- 'put, bestow' (dhā-) beside *deh₃- (dātár- in RV 8.51.5). Greek ἐΰς survives as an adjective only in formulae, which is why the gen. pl. ἐάων is archaic.
shared_syntax: Gods (subject / vocative) + give/bestow + 'goods' (acc. pl. or gen. pl. with agent noun) + dative of the worshipper: Ved. asmai dhatta vasavo vasūni; Gk θεοὶ δέ τοι ὄλβια δοῖεν; θεοὶ δωτῆρες ἐάων.
context: Prayer/blessing contexts in all: AVŚ 7.97.6 (Vasus asked to give goods to the sacrificer), AVP 19.44.41 (Agni as householder, 'be the bestower of goods'), HH Ap. 466 (blessing on a stranger, 'may the gods give you prosperity'), Od. 8.325 (gods as 'givers of goods'). The exact agent-noun formula in three branches (support) makes chance unlikely; the packet itself holds the Vedic side fully and the Greek side only in renewed form.
phrase: *déh₃tores h₁wésuōm 'givers of goods' / *h₁wésu dʰeh₁- 'bestow goods' (pie-lex-deh3toxr + pie-lex-h1wesus; pie-root-dheh1-do)

support.locus: RV 7.7.4c (packet: viśā́m ... viśpátiḥ, the parallel *wiḱ-pótis compound)

cognate: Ved. dám-pati- = Gk δεσ-πότης (= Av. dəṇg paiti-, recalled): gen. *dem-s 'of the house' + *pótis 'master'.
drift_or_renewal: Vedic dual dámpatī = 'master and mistress of the house, the married couple' (AVP 19.55.17 blessing the couple with prosperity); Greek δεσπότης drifted to 'master (of slaves), lord' (Hec. 617 the new masters of the captive women).
shared_syntax: Fossilized genitive + head noun (old root-noun genitive *dems not otherwise productive in either language).
context: Both refer to the person(s) in authority over a household; the Vedic is a domestic ritual blessing, the Greek a household of captives. A frozen syntagm rather than a poetic formula; certain as inheritance, weak as phraseology.

cognate: Only the privative *n̥- (Ved. a-, Lat. in-); the 'see' roots differ (Ved. dṛś < *derḱ-, Lat. uid- < *weyd-).
drift_or_renewal: Root renewed in one branch; the merism shape 'seen and unseen' with privative is kept. Lat. inuisus here = 'unseen' (not the usual 'hated'), an archaic sense kept in the prayer formula.
shared_syntax: Polar merism: participle + privative participle of a 'see' verb, as a totalizing designation of harmful agents (acc. pl. object of 'ward off / kill').
context: Both in apotropaic healing/protective ritual: AVŚ 6.52 (sun 'slayer of the unseen', cows settled in the pen, unseen vermin trapped) and the related AVŚ 5.23 / AVP 5.3 (kill the seen and unseen worms); Cato 141.2 Mars asked to ward off 'diseases seen and unseen' from farm and herd. The referent (disease agents) and the genre agree, but X/un-X merisms are productive in both languages, so inheritance is uncertain.
